draft.title: Goods and services
card: things you can touch and own, such as food or a phone. Once bought, the good belongs to the customer.
work done for people, such as tourism, education or streaming. The customer gets the result but does not take home a physical item.
Both goods and services are bought and sold between places in trade. A country can export phones, and it can also sell education to overseas students.
To tell them apart, ask: does the customer leave owning a physical item, or did someone do work for them? Streaming a film is a service, even though you watch it on a phone.
draft.remember: A good is a thing you own. A service is work done for you.

a.q: Why is watching a film on a streaming service a service and not a good?
opts: It is work done for the customer, not an item they own
It costs less than the physical items most shops sell
It is sold by a large company and not a small business
It is paid for before the customer uses it
a.why: Streaming is work done for the customer, and they do not take home a physical item to own. Price, business size and when it is paid for do not decide whether something is a good or a service.
a.clue: Does the customer end up owning a thing they can touch?

b.q: Priya runs a bike shop in Parramatta, NSW. She sells new bikes and also tunes up bikes by adjusting the gears and brakes. Which is correct?
opts: The bikes are goods and the tune-ups are a service
The bikes are a service and the tune-ups are goods
Both are services, as staff help customers choose
Both are goods, as tune-ups are done on a bike
b.why: A new bike is a physical item the customer owns, so it is a good. A tune-up is work done on a bike the customer already owns, so it is a service. Being done on a physical item does not turn a tune-up into a good.
b.clue: What does the customer own after each sale that they did not own before?

a.best: It is work done for the customer, not an item they own

b.best: The bikes are goods and the tune-ups are a service
